# AF 第八章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 8

[P01] A few days later, the fear went away. Some animals remembered the Sixth Commandment（戒律）: "No animal shall kill any other animal." No one wanted to say this to the pigs or dogs. They felt the killings（杀戮） did not agree with it. Clover asked Benjamin to read it. He said he would not get involved（卷入）. So she got Muriel. Muriel read: "No animal shall kill any other animal WITHOUT CAUSE." The last two words had gone from their memory.

[P02] But now they saw the Commandment was not broken. They had a good reason to kill the traitors who had joined Snowball. All that year the animals worked harder than before. They had to rebuild the windmill（风车） with walls twice as thick, and finish it on time, and also do the usual farm work. This was tremendous（极大的） work. Sometimes they felt they worked longer hours and ate no better than in Jones's day. On Sunday mornings Squealer held a long strip（剥去） of paper and read out lists of numbers. These proved that the production of every kind of food had gone up by two hundred, three hundred, or five hundred per cent.

[P03] The animals did not doubt him. They could not remember what life was like before the uprising（起义）. Some days they felt they would rather have less numbers and more food. Now all orders came from Squealer or another pig. Napoleon was not seen in public often, not even once every two weeks. When he did appear, dogs walked with him, and a black cockerel（小公鸡） marched in front and acted like a trumpeter.

[P04] People said Napoleon lived in separate rooms in the farmhouse（农舍）. He ate alone, and two dogs served him. He always used the Crown（王冠） Derby（德比） dinner service from the glass cupboard（橱柜）. They also said a gun would be fired every year on his birthday. No one just called him "Napoleon" now. They called him "our Leader, Comrade（同志） Napoleon." The pigs liked to make up titles for him, like Father of All Animals, Terror of Mankind, Protector of the Sheep, Ducklings' Friend, and more.

[P05] In his speeches, Squealer would cry and talk about Napoleon's wisdom, his good heart, and his deep love for all animals, even the sad ones who still lived in slavery（奴役） on other farms. People thanked Napoleon for every success and every piece of good luck. One hen would say to another, "Under our Leader, Comrade Napoleon, I have laid five eggs in six days." Two cows at the pool would say, "Thanks to Comrade Napoleon, how good this water tastes!" A poem by Minimus, Comrade Napoleon, showed the general feeling: Friend of fatherless（无父）!

[P06] Fountain（喷泉） of happiness! Lord（老爷） of the swill（泔水）-bucket! Oh, my soul is on fire when I look at your calm, strong eye, like the sun, Comrade Napoleon! You give what animals love: a full belly（肚子） twice a day, clean straw（稻草）. Every animal, great or small, sleeps in peace. You watch over all, Comrade Napoleon! Even a sucking（吸奶）-pig should learn to be true to you, and his first squeak（叫声） should be "Comrade Napoleon!" Napoleon liked this poem and had it written on the barn（谷仓） wall, opposite the Seven Commandments（戒律）.

[P07] Above it was a picture of Napoleon, in profile（侧面）, painted by Squealer in white paint. Meanwhile（同时）, Napoleon was talking with Frederick and Pilkington about business through Whymper. The timber（木材） was still not sold. Frederick wanted it more, but would not pay a fair price. There were new rumours（谣言） that Frederick planned to attack Animal Farm and destroy the windmill, because he was jealous. People knew Snowball was hiding on Pinchfield（窄地） Farm. In the middle of the summer, the animals heard that three hens said Snowball had planned to kill Napoleon.

[P08] They were killed at once, and new ways kept Napoleon safe. Four dogs guarded his bed at night. A young pig named Pinkeye（红眼） tasted all his food in case it was poisoned（中毒）. People were told Napoleon would sell the timber to Mr. Pilkington, and make a deal to exchange products with Foxwood（狐林）. Napoleon and Pilkington were almost friendly, though they only talked through Whymper.

[P09] The animals did not trust Pilkington, but they liked him much more than Frederick. They feared and hated Frederick. As summer went on, the windmill was almost finished, and more people talked about a coming attack. People said Frederick wanted to bring twenty men with guns. He had given money to the judges and police. So if he got the papers for Animal Farm, they would ask no questions. Also, terrible stories came from Pinchfield about how cruel Frederick was to his animals. He had beaten an old horse to death, he did not give his cows food, he had killed a dog by throwing it into a fire, and he made cocks（公鸡） fight with sharp（锋利） blades（刀片） tied to their spurs（马刺）.

[P10] When the animals heard what happened to their friends, they were very angry. Sometimes they shouted that they wanted to attack Pinchfield Farm, drive the humans away, and set the animals free. But Squealer told them not to act quickly and to trust Comrade Napoleon's plan. Still, many animals felt angry at Frederick. One Sunday morning Napoleon came to the barn and said he had never thought of selling the wood to Frederick. He said it was below him to deal with bad men like that.

[P11] The pigeons still went out to tell others about the uprising. They were told not to go to Foxwood and to stop saying "Death to Humanity（人类）." Instead they said "Death to Frederick." In late summer, another bad plan of Snowball was found out. The wheat was full of weeds（杂草）. Snowball had come at night and mixed weed seeds with the seed corn. A gander（雄鹅） knew about the plan. He told Squealer he was guilty, then killed himself by eating poison（毒药） berries（浆果）. The animals also learned that Snowball had never won "Animal Hero, First Class." It was only a story spread later by Snowball after the Battle of the Cowshed（牛棚）.

[P12] He was not given a medal. Instead, he was blamed（责备） for being a coward（懦夫） in the battle. Some animals were confused again, but Squealer soon made them believe their memories were wrong. In the autumn, the windmill was finished. It took a huge, tiring（累人） effort, because the harvest had to be gathered（聚集） at almost the same time. The machines still had to be put in, and Whymper was talking about buying them, but the building itself was done.

[P13] They worked very hard. They had no experience, only simple tools, bad luck and Snowball's betrayal（背叛）. But they finished the work on the exact（确切） day! They were tired but proud. They walked round their great building. Moreover, the walls were twice as thick as before. Only explosives（炸药） could break them now! They thought about their hard work and the problems they had overcome（克服）. They thought about how different their lives would be when the sails turned and the machines ran. Then their tiredness（疲劳） left them. They jumped and ran round the windmill, shouting with joy.

[P14] Napoleon came down with his dogs and his cockerel to look at the finished work. He thanked the animals and said the mill（磨坊） would be called Napoleon Mill. Two days later, the animals had a special meeting in the barn. Napoleon said he had sold the timber to Frederick. Tomorrow Frederick's wagons（货车） would come and take it away. All along, while Napoleon seemed friendly with Pilkington, he had really been in secret agreement with Frederick. All relations with Foxwood were broken, and insulting（侮辱） messages were sent to Pilkington.

[P15] The pigeons were told to stay away from Pinchfield Farm and to change their slogan from "Death to Frederick" to "Death to Pilkington."Napoleon also said the stories of an attack were not true, and the tales about Frederick's cruelty were exaggerated（夸大）. These rumours probably came from Snowball, who was not on Pinchfield Farm and had never been there: he was living well at Foxwood, paid by Pilkington for years. The pigs were happy about Napoleon's clever plan.

[P16] By acting friendly with Pilkington, Napoleon made Frederick pay twelve pounds more. But Squealer said Napoleon was very clever because he trusted nobody, not even Frederick. Frederick wanted to pay for the wood with a cheque（支票）—a piece of paper promising to pay. But Napoleon was too clever. He wanted real five-pound notes before the wood was taken away. Frederick had already paid. The money was just enough to buy the machines for the windmill. Meanwhile the wood was taken away quickly.

[P17] When the wood was gone, the animals had a meeting. They came to look at Frederick's bank-notes. Napoleon smiled and wore his two medals. He rested on straw on the platform（舞台）, with the money beside him. The animals walked past and looked at it. Boxer put out his nose to smell the notes. The thin paper moved. Three days later there was a big noise. Whymper came fast on his bicycle. His face was very white. He ran into the farmhouse.

[P18] Then a loud angry cry came from Napoleon's room. The money was not real! Frederick had taken the wood for nothing! Napoleon called the animals together. In a terrible voice he said Frederick must die. He warned them that worse was coming. Frederick and his men might attack at any moment. Guards were placed on all roads. Four pigeons were sent to Foxwood with a friendly message for Pilkington. The next morning the attack came.

[P19] The animals were eating breakfast when the look-outs ran in. They said Frederick and his men had come through the five-barred（阻挡） gate. The animals went out bravely to meet them. But this time they did not win easily. There were fifteen men with six guns. They fired when they were fifty yards away. The animals could not face the loud bangs（巨响） and the stinging（刺痛） pellets（颗粒）. Napoleon and Boxer tried to rally（集会） them, but they were soon driven back. Some were already wounded.

[P20] They hid in the farm buildings and looked out through small holes. The field and the windmill now belonged to the enemy. Even Napoleon did not know what to do. He walked up and down and said nothing. His tail was shaking. They looked sadly toward Foxwood. If Pilkington and his men helped them, they might still win. But then the four pigeons came back. One carried a small piece of paper from Pilkington. It said: "Serves you right." Meanwhile Frederick and his men had stopped near the windmill.

[P21] The animals watched, very upset. Two men had a crowbar（铁撬） and a big hammer（锤子）. They wanted to knock the windmill down, but he said, "Impossible!""Impossible!" cried Napoleon. "Our walls are too thick. They cannot knock it down in a week. Be brave, comrades（同志们）!" But Benjamin watched closely. The men made a hole near the bottom. Benjamin nodded his long nose slowly. He looked almost amused（逗乐）. "I thought so," he said.

[P22] "In another moment they will put blasting（爆破） powder（火药） into that hole." The animals were very afraid. They could not go out now. The men ran in all directions. Then there was a very loud roar（吼叫）. The pigeons flew up. All the animals except Napoleon threw themselves flat and hid their faces. When they got up, a big cloud of black smoke hung where the windmill had been. Slowly the wind blew it away. The windmill was gone! At this sight, the animals felt brave again.

[P23] Their fear and sadness were gone. They were very angry and shouted for revenge（复仇）. They did not wait for orders and ran straight at the enemy. This time they did not care about the cruel pellets. It was a hard battle. The men fired again and again. When the animals came close, the men hit them with sticks and boots. A cow, three sheep, and two geese were killed. Almost everyone was hurt. Even Napoleon had the tip（尖端） of his tail hit by a pellet（弹丸）.

[P24] But the men were hurt too. Boxer's hoofs（蹄） broke three men's heads. A cow's horn gored（刺伤） one man in the belly. Jessie and Bluebell nearly tore off another man's trousers. Napoleon had told his nine dogs to hide behind the hedge（树篱）. Now they suddenly appeared at the men's side, barking fiercely, and the men were very afraid. They saw they might be surrounded（包围）. Frederick shouted to his men to run away while they could, and the cowardly（胆小） enemy ran for their lives. The animals chased（追赶） them to the bottom of the field and kicked them as they pushed through the thorn（荆棘） hedge. They had won, but they were tired and bleeding.

[P25] They limped（跛行） back to the farm and cried for their dead friends. They stopped in sad silence where the windmill once stood. It was gone, and even its base was broken. The fallen stones were thrown far away, and they could not build it again. It was like the windmill had never been there. When they came near the farm, Squealer came jumping to them, wagging（摇摆） his tail and looking very pleased.

[P26] The animals heard a gun from the farm. "What is that gun for?" said Boxer. "To celebrate our victory!" cried Squealer. "What victory?" said Boxer. His knees were bleeding. He lost a shoe and his hoof（蹄） was split（分裂）. "What victory, comrade? Did we not drive the enemy off our land?" "But they destroyed the windmill. We worked on it for two years!" "What does it matter? We will build another windmill. We will build six windmills（风车） if we want.

[P27] "You do not understand, comrade, the great thing we have done. The enemy held this very ground we stand on. Now, thanks to Comrade Napoleon, we have won it all back!" "Then we have won back what we had before," said Boxer. "That is our victory," said Boxer.said Squealer. They limped into the yard. The small shots under the skin（皮肤） of Boxer's leg hurt badly. He saw ahead the heavy work of building the windmill again, and in his mind he got ready. But for the first time he thought that he was eleven years old and that perhaps his big muscles（肌肉） were not as they once were. But when the animals saw the green flag flying, and heard the gun firing again—seven times in all—and heard Napoleon's speech, praising them, it did seem to them that they had won a great victory.

[P28] The animals killed in the battle had a solemn（庄严） funeral. Boxer and Clover pulled the wagon（货车）, and Napoleon walked in front. They celebrated for two days with songs, speeches, and gun firing. Every animal got a gift: an apple, two ounces（盎司） of corn for birds, and three biscuits for dogs. They named it the Battle of the Windmill, and Napoleon gave himself a new medal, the Order of the Green Banner（横幅）.

[P29] After the party, everyone forgot the trouble about the banknotes（钞票）. A few days later, the pigs found a box of whisky（威士忌） in the farmhouse cellar（地窖）. That night, loud singing came from the farmhouse. It mixed with the song 'Animals of England'. At about half past nine, Napoleon came out of the back door. He wore an old bowler hat of Mr. Jones. He ran round the yard and went back inside.

[P30] But in the morning the farmhouse was quiet. It was almost nine when Squealer came out. He walked slowly, his eyes were dull（沉闷）, his tail hung down. He called the animals together and told them he had terrible news. Napoleon was dying（垂死）! The animals cried. They put straw outside the door and walked on tiptoe（踮脚）. With tears, they asked what they should do if their Leader was taken away.

[P31] A rumour（谣言） went round that Snowball had put poison in Napoleon's food. At eleven o'clock Squealer came out with another announcement（宣布）. Napoleon's last act was a solemn decree（法令）: drinking alcohol（酒精） was to be punished by death. By the evening, Napoleon seemed a little better. The next morning Squealer said he was getting well. That evening Napoleon was back at work. The next day, they learned Napoleon had told Whymper to buy some booklets on brewing and distilling in Willingdon.

[P32] A week later Napoleon said the small field past the orchard（果园） must be ploughed. Before, old animals ate grass there. People were told the grass was used up. But soon everyone knew Napoleon wanted to plant barley（大麦） there. One night at twelve there was a loud crash（碰撞） in the yard, and the animals ran out.

[P33] It was a night with the moon. At the end wall of the big barn, where the Seven Commandments were written, a ladder lay broken in two. Squealer was lying（躺） beside it. Near him there was a lantern, a paint-brush, and a pot of white paint turned over. The dogs made a ring round Squealer, and took him back to the farmhouse. No animal could understand what this meant, except old Benjamin. He nodded his muzzle（口鼻部） as if he knew, but said nothing. A few days later Muriel noticed that there was another commandment which the animals had remembered wrong.

[P34] They remembered it as "No animal shall drink alcohol." But they forgot two words: "TO EXCESS（过量）."
